lateral border of humerus: Lateral border of the humerus; below it continues as the lateral supracondylar ridge.
lateral border of scapula: Lateral border facing the axilla; teres major and minor arise from it.
lateral condyle of femur: Lateral condyle of the femur; forms the knee joint with the tibia and meniscus, and its forward prominence prevents lateral slipping of the patella.
lateral condyle of tibia: Lateral condyle of the tibia; the lateral meniscus rests on it.
lateral crico-arytenoid muscle: Pulls the muscular process of the arytenoid forwards, bringing the vocal folds together (adduction); recurrent laryngeal nerve.
lateral cuneiform bone: Medium-sized cuneiform; it lies between the cuboid and the 3rd metatarsal.
lateral epicondyle of femur: Prominence on the lateral condyle; the lateral collateral ligament and the lateral head of gastrocnemius attach to it.
lateral epicondyle of humerus: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus; common origin of the forearm extensors (tennis elbow).
lateral femoral intermuscular septum: Fascial wall separating the anterior and posterior thigh compartments laterally.
lateral head of flexor hallucis brevis: Lateral head of flexor hallucis brevis
Head attaching to the lateral sesamoid.
lateral head of gastrocnemius: Calf head arising from the lateral condyle of the femur.
lateral head of triceps brachii: Head arising above the radial groove; supplied by the radial nerve.
lateral intercondylar tubercle: Lateral tubercle of the intercondylar eminence.
lateral intermuscular septum of arm: The radial nerve pierces this septum to enter the anterior compartment.
lateral lip of linea aspera: Lateral lip of the linea aspera; vastus lateralis and the short head of biceps femoris attach to it.
lateral malleolar facet: Triangular surface that articulates with the lateral malleolus.
lateral malleolus: Lower end of the fibula; it reaches further down and further back than the medial malleolus.
lateral mass: Thick lateral part of the atlas on each side; transfers weight from the skull to the axis.
lateral meniscus: Nearly O-shaped lateral meniscus; it does not attach to the collateral ligament, is linked to popliteus and is more mobile.
lateral part of occipital bone: Part beside the foramen magnum; carries the condyles.
lateral part of sacrum: Lateral parts of the sacrum; they carry the alae and the auricular surfaces.
lateral part of transverse process: Outer part of the transverse process.
lateral patellar retinaculum: Extension of the vastus lateralis aponeurosis from the edge of the patella to the tibia.
lateral process of calcaneal tuberosity: Lateral process of the calcaneal tuberosity; abductor digiti minimi arises here.
lateral process of malleus: Small process of the malleus that makes a bulge on the eardrum.
lateral process of nasal septal cartilag: Lateral process of septal cartilage (upper lateral cartilage)
Cartilage plate extending sideways from the septal cartilage, supporting the middle of the nasal dorsum (upper lateral cartilage).
lateral process of talus: Lateral process of the talus; site of the snowboarder's fracture.
lateral pterygoid muscle: Its upper and lower heads attach to the mandibular condyle and the articular disc; the muscle of mastication that opens the mouth and protrudes the jaw.
lateral pterygoid plate: Lateral plate of the pterygoid process; both pterygoid muscles arise from it.
lateral rectus muscle: Muscle that turns the eye outwards (abduction); supplied by the abducens nerve (VI). Its paralysis causes a convergent squint and horizontal double vision.
lateral sacral crest: Ridge formed by the fused transverse processes; the sacrotuberous ligament attaches to it.
lateral subtendinous bursa of gastrocnem: Between the lateral head and the capsule.
lateral supracondylar line: Continuation of the linea aspera down to the lateral condyle; plantaris and the lateral head of gastrocnemius arise from it.
lateral supracondylar ridge: Ridge above the lateral epicondyle; brachioradialis and ECRL arise from it.
lateral surface of fibula: Lateral surface of the fibula; fibularis longus and brevis arise from it.
lateral surface of radius: Lateral surface of the radius; pronator teres inserts at its middle.
lateral surface of tibia: Lateral surface of the tibia; tibialis anterior arises from it.
lateral talocalcaneal ligament: Short ligament joining the lateral surfaces of the talus and calcaneus.
lateral temporomandibular ligament: Lateral thickening of the capsule; prevents backward displacement of the condyle.
lateral thyrohyoid ligament: Joins the superior horn of the thyroid cartilage to the greater horn of the hyoid; a small triticeous cartilage may lie within it.
lateral tubercle: Lateral tubercle of the posterior process of the talus; the posterior talofibular ligament attaches to it.
latissimus dorsi muscle: Broad flat muscle from the lower back to the floor of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus; adducts, extends and medially rotates the arm. Nerve: thoracodorsal nerve (C6–C8).
lenticular process of incus: Lens-shaped process at the tip of the long limb; articulates with the stapes.
lesser horn of hyoid bone: Lesser horn; the stylohyoid ligament attaches to it.
lesser sciatic foramen: Lesser sciatic foramen; the obturator internus tendon, the pudendal nerve and the internal pudendal vessels pass through it.
lesser sciatic notch: Notch below the ischial spine; ligaments convert it into the lesser sciatic foramen.
lesser trochanter: Projection on the posteromedial side of the femoral neck; iliopsoas inserts here.
lesser tubercle: Small prominence on the front of the humerus; subscapularis inserts here.
lesser wing: Small wing surrounding the optic canal; forms the posterior border of the anterior cranial fossa.
levator anguli oris: Runs from the canine fossa to the corner of the mouth; raises the corner of the mouth.
levator ani: Pelvic floor muscle made up of pubococcygeus, puboanalis and iliococcygeus; it supports the pelvic organs and contributes to continence. S4 and branches of the pudendal nerve.
levator labii superioris: Runs from below the orbital margin to the upper lip; raises the upper lip.
levator nasolabialis: Runs from the frontal process of the maxilla to the ala of the nose and the upper lip.
levator palpebrae superioris: Muscle that raises the upper eyelid; supplied by the oculomotor nerve, while its smooth-muscle fibres (superior tarsal muscle) are sympathetic. Its paralysis causes ptosis.
levator scapulae: Runs from the transverse processes of C1–C4 to the superior angle of the scapula; elevates the scapula. Nerves: dorsal scapular nerve and C3–C4.
levatores breves costarum: Small muscles from the transverse processes to the rib immediately below.
levatores longi costarum: Small muscles from the transverse processes that skip one rib to reach the second rib below.
